general.title: General
general.languageHint: It changes right away and is remembered.

agents.title: Agents
agents.description: brnch looks for each agent on this machine and checks it with its own command.
agents.pendingVerification: Flags and output format still to be verified
agents.ownKey: Each agent's login or API key is its own and it needs it to work. brnch protects git credentials, not the agent's.
agents.defaultAgentHint: Preselected when you create a run.
agents.defaultPermissionHint: What an agent may do without asking you.

security.title: Security
security.description: Agents do not need your git token to publish. Here you see whether they can be confined.
security.activeHint: Agents start confined. If isolation stopped being available, they would not run.
security.inactive: No isolation available: agents will not run
security.unknown: The state could not be read.
security.agentKey: The agent's own login or API key is out of scope: it needs it to work.

items.agent: The keys of your SSH agent

security.neverUnconfined: Do not run agents without isolation
security.neverUnconfinedHint: If no isolation is available, the agent does not start. It cannot be turned off.
security.measuredNote: "Check now" leaves a test file in your home folder, asks a confined process to read it and removes it. It measures this machine, right now.
security.measuredWritable: The confined agent could still write in its workspace.
security.measuredNotWritable: The confined agent could NOT write in its workspace.

windows.setupHint: Creates the local account agents run under. Windows asks for administrator permission once.
windows.keyHint: The agent runs as another account, so it does not see your Claude login. Give it an API key; it is kept protected for you and passed only to the agent.
windows.keySaved: Saved. New agents will receive it.

connections.title: Connections
connections.description: The accounts and credentials gitd publishes with. gitd keeps them; agents never receive them.
connections.needsGitd: gitd has to be running to manage connections.
connections.agentsNever: Agents never receive this credential: gitd keeps it and pushes branches for them.

kind.github_login: github.com · GitHub sign-in · pull requests are opened as you

github.title: Sign in with GitHub
github.description: The quickest. You authorise on github.com with whichever account you want.
github.one: You pick the account on GitHub, not here
github.two: No tokens or keys to copy
github.three: Pull requests are opened as you

ssh.title: SSH key
ssh.description: brnch creates a key for this computer and you add it to your account.
ssh.one: It does not expire like a token
ssh.two: You add it by hand on GitHub

token.title: Access token
token.description: You paste a personal token that you create on GitHub.
token.one: Works if your organisation does not allow apps
token.three: It expires: you will have to renew it

github.waiting: Waiting for you to authorise on GitHub…

one.title: Press “Open GitHub”
one.hint: If you are not signed in, GitHub asks you to.

two.title: Choose your account and enter the code
two.hint: With several accounts or organisations, this is where you decide which one.

three.title: Press “Authorize”
three.hint: brnch notices by itself; you do not press anything here.

github.connected: Connected. gitd will publish as your GitHub account and pull requests will be opened as you.
github.reachHint: Only those you choose on GitHub when installing gitd's app. You can give all or just some, and change it whenever you like.

token.prefixHint: A specific organisation or user, or https://github.com/ for all of them.
token.label: Access token
token.handed: brnch hands it to gitd once and never sees it again. It is not kept in any brnch file.
token.fineGrained: A fine-grained token limited to the repositories you use is best.
token.expires: Tokens expire. When one stops working you will have to replace it.

ssh.private: Fingerprint {{fingerprint}} · The private key stays in brnch's data folder, readable only by your user. Agents never see it.
ssh.addTitle: Add it to your GitHub account
ssh.addHint: Press the button, paste the key, give it a title like “brnch · my PC” and choose “Authentication key”.
ssh.ok: GitHub recognises the key. gitd will read and publish over SSH.
ssh.refused: GitHub does not recognise the key yet. Add it on GitHub and check again; until then gitd does not use it.
